Restated before interest: AZN paid $3,710mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 2.34% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 1.30% to 0.00%. Restated at replacement capex: AZN spent $6,095mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $2,411mm of plant depreciation, 2.32% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge stays nil. Restated with selling costs: SG&A now carries AZN's filed selling or distribution costs, 0.99% of revenue this charge was absorbing, so it falls from 0.00% to nil. The filed lines alone now leave less than the cash the company made before interest and at replacement capex, and a charge below nil would credit the book with cash its own costs do not leave. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 22.75% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 27.47%, so the charge rebuilds at -4.72%. It was held at nil, but AZN books $4,207mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0001104659-26-019130), 7.16% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -4.72%. Checked without working capital build: no change in payables on file from the cash flow statement for every year, so the charge stands.

GSK states that approximately 70% of US COPD patients inadequately controlled on inhaled triple therapy who continue to exacerbate have a blood eosinophil count of 150 cells/uL and above, and that this group represents over a million people (GSK release 2025-05-22, citing GSK Optum Analysis DOF 2024N562932_00 and Mullerova H et al., Int J Chron Obstruct Pulmon Dis 2019). So the all-eosinophil exacerbating pool is 1,000,000 / 0.70 = 1,428,571, and 1,428,571 / 14,200,000 diagnosed US COPD adults = 0.1006. That is the OBERON and TITANIA entry criterion
column12: cross-checked: Sanofi puts the Dupixent COPD label pool at approximately 300,000 US adults at 300 cells/uL and above, which is 21% of the 1,428,571, against a measured 26.6% at that threshold in 34,391 US COPD patients (Mullerova 2019). The chain is consistent within about 25%. It leans low, because GSK's denominator is triple therapy while the trials enrolled inhaled standard care including dual

column11: stated equal to prevalence, which sets the engine's carryover to zero, so the penetration is the share of each year's eligible patients started rather than a share of an accumulating pool
column12: THIS IS THE WEAKEST INPUT IN THE ROW AND IT IS A CONVENTION, NOT A MEASUREMENT. COPD is not a disease whose prevalent pool turns over annually, the way idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is, and no US COPD incidence sits beside the BRFSS prevalence. The solve behind the penetration assumes a constant eligible pool each year, which is what this produces. State a real incidence and the penetration has to be re-solved

column11: Tezspire's measured class capture, at a 1.0 multiple. Tezspire held 16.94% of the US biologic asthma class in 2024 (13,837 Medicare beneficiaries of 81,661 across Tezspire, Nucala, Fasenra and Xolair), and 11.9% of severe asthma patients are on any biologic (Park et al., J Asthma Allergy 2026;19, doi 10.2147/JAA.S580937, 2,827 patients, 5.2% at GINA step 4 and 19.6% at step 5). 0.119 x 0.1694 = 2.02% of the pool, solved back through the curve and a 25.4% discontinuation to a peak of 0.02039
column12: the 1.0 multiple is a judgement, argued from OBERON and TITANIA cutting exacerbations 29% and 34% across all eosinophil counts against Dupixent at 300 cells/uL and above and Nucala at 150 and above. TWO DISCLOSURES, BOTH POINTING DOWN. Dupixent is absent from the class denominator at 88,374 Part D beneficiaries that cannot be split across its six indications, and it is the actual COPD competitor, so including any of it cuts Tezspire's share. And Park's 11.9% is a 2018 to 2021 baseline being applied to a 2028 launch
